newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar firms on U.S. consumer price data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar firms on U.S. consumer price data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar firmed to C$1.3696 (US$0.7302) from Thursday's close of C$1.3716 (US$0.7291) after U.S. consumer price data hinted at low inflationary pressure, dealers said. * The currency will likely remain range bound into next week as investors keep a wary eye on rate spreads between Canada and the United States, dealers said.
Canada's consumer price index clocked in as expected. The index rose 1.4 percent in August on a yearly basis, after a rise of 1.2 percent the previous month.
But market players continue to be wary of the Bank of Canada's monetary policy, said dealers. The market fears a widening spread between Canadian and U.S. rates.
"The bottom line is that the Canada is still range bound," said one dealer.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.1047 marks from Thursday's close of 1.1022 marks, and rose to 80.57 yen from 80.26 yen.
